title: Store ownership: one deep .mulch store module (lenient | strict | raw-line policies, compact rewrite)
description:
Architecture gate (sprint 3, report candidate 1, Strong). Evidence: the lib `Store` has ZERO callers in the binary; six readers and five writers implement the same file conventions independently (commands/mod.rs raw-line IO, status/validate/doctor lenient reads, records.rs strict reader/writer, ConfigStore writing mulch.config.yaml itself). Problem: the format contract lives in prose + duplicated IO; every one of the ~20 remaining parity commands needs another read+write of the same store. Solution: name the access policies (lenient | strict | raw-line for reads; rewrite-compact | append-verbatim for writes) in the lib store module and move the CLI's file IO behind them, starting with one pilot command (status). Benefits: locality (the reference semantics live in one place), leverage (each new command inherits the policies), tests (policy-level unit tests replace per-command store fixtures). Note: README DEVIATIONS pins the lenient/strict reader split as CONTRACT — the deepening must name both policies, never merge them. title: record upsert semantics: named-type duplicates update in place (not an anonymous advisory)
description:
Parity gap found by the sprint-4 spec review (battery-blind; pre-existing since mulch-fdd0). Reference `commands/record.ts:1085-1130`: a duplicate on pattern/decision/reference/guide UPSERTS in place and prints `✓ Updated existing <type> in <domain> (record #N)`; the batch path reports `updated` in its counters. Ours always prints `Duplicate <type> already exists in <domain> (record #N). Use --force to add anyway.` and writes nothing; batch counts it as `skipped`. Also: the dedupe key is wrong — the reference `findDuplicate` (utils/expertise.ts:194-217) compares the TYPE'S DEDUP FIELD, ours compares the id, so a store holding a renamed record (which `edit --name` produces, since neither side recomputes ids) gets a second appended record where the reference upserts one. Evidence: 3-way probes in the sprint-4 spec review (/tmp/review, report lines 2-3).

SPRINT 6 PICK (2026-10-04): bug before features — same data-integrity class as mulch-b88b (wrong store shape on the write path: duplicate append where the reference upserts one record, plus the wrong dedupe key compounds after edit --name renames). 351d/ca49/9e70 follow.

title: Store writer lock: flock on .mulch/.lock around load->mutate->save — parallel mulch processes silently lose records
description:
CONTEXT (2026-10-15, user request: port the seeds-0d7b writer lock to mulch):

- mulch (sprint-28 tree) does read-modify-write over .mulch/expertise/<domain>.jsonl (+ mulch.config.yaml for domain registration/auto-create) with NO inter-process exclusion: two mulch processes (two agents recording, record racing doctor --fix) both load, both rewrite_domain, the last rename wins and the other's records are silently lost (lost update). Same class as the fabro-4cfc tracker incident.
- The REFERENCE ml 0.10.7 has its own lock: utils/lock.ts withFileLock — PER-FILE O_CREAT|O_EXCL lockfile at `<file>.lock`, 50ms retry, 5s timeout (error: "Timed out waiting for lock on <path>. If no other mulch process is running, delete the lock file manually."), 30s mtime-staleness recovery, held around the whole read->dedupe->upsert->write cycle (record.ts:388ff); dry-run reads run lock-free; hooks fire outside the lock. move.ts even nests target+source locks (deadlock-prone ordering).
- Weakness of the reference form (why we deviate): a crashed holder leaves the lockfile — writers wedge up to 30s or until manual deletion; the staleness-steal can in principle double-admit a >30s holder. seeds (denkhaus/seeds, seeds-0d7b, shipped in seeds 0.8.0) solved exactly this store-wide with flock: advisory exclusive lock on .seeds/.lock via std::fs::File::try_lock, kernel-owned (released on process death — no stale-lockfile machinery), 5s acquire timeout, 25ms poll, Error::LockTimeout, Store::open_exclusive acquires BEFORE the first read and holds until drop. Proven code: crates/seeds/src/lock.rs + tests/writer_lock.rs (8 parallel creates keep every record; holder death proceeds immediately; reads never create the lock file).

DEMAND:
1. Port the seeds WriterLock as a LIB module (mulch::lock): advisory exclusive flock on `.mulch/.lock` (create + !truncate, permanent zero-byte sibling), acquired BEFORE the store's first read, held until the StoreFiles drops — the whole load->mutate->save cycle of a mutating command is atomic against other mulch processes. Store-wide granularity deliberately: one lock covers domain file + config mutations as one transaction (the reference's per-file lock leaves the domain auto-create config race open) and sidesteps move's nested-lock ordering.
